messages.content:
Work over \(\mathbb C\). A rank-\(r\) algebraic vector bundle \(E\) on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\) is called uniform if there are integers \(a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_r\) such that, for every projective line \(L\subset\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\),
\[
E|_L\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_L(a_i),
\]
where \(\mathcal O_L(a)\) denotes the line bundle of degree \(a\) on \(L\cong\mathbb P^1\). Call \(E\) homogeneous if \(g^*E\cong E\) for every projective linear automorphism \(g\in\operatorname{PGL}_{n+1}(\mathbb C)\).

Determine the exact value of
\[
d=\min\left\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\text{there exists a uniform, non-homogeneous algebraic vector bundle on }\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\text{ of some rank }1\le r<2n\right\},
\]
with the convention \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\).

content.text:
This is an open problem: the requested value of \(d\) is not currently known.

The **homogeneity conjecture for uniform bundles on projective space** asserts that every uniform vector bundle on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\) of rank \(r<2n\) is homogeneous. Thus:
- \(d=+\infty\) would establish that conjecture;
- any finite value of \(d\) would identify the smallest-dimensional counterexample.

Non-homogeneous uniform bundles are known in rank \(2n\), but that rank is excluded by the strict inequality in the question. Those examples therefore do not determine \(d\).

\[
\boxed{\text{The exact value of }d\text{ is unknown.}}
\]

import sympy as s
# A nondegenerate bivector on a six-dimensional vector space.
N=6
J=s.zeros(N)
for i in range(0,N,2):
    J[i,i+1]=1
    J[i+1,i]=-1
# Infinitesimal GL(V) orbit of the projective class of J.
pairs=[(i,j) for i in range(N) for j in range(i+1,N)]
cols=[]
for a in range(N):
    for b in range(N):
        X=s.zeros(N); X[a,b]=1
        Y=X*J+J*X.T
        cols.append(s.Matrix([Y[i,j] for i,j in pairs]))
M=s.Matrix.hstack(*cols)
v=s.Matrix([J[i,j] for i,j in pairs])
print('rank of bivector:',J.rank())
print('rank of bundle: binomial(5,2)-1 =',s.binomial(5,2)-1)
print('line splitting: O(1)^4 + O^5')
print('dimension of orbit in projective bivectors:',M.row_join(v).rank()-1)
print('dimension of projective stabilizer:',35-(M.row_join(v).rank()-1))

content.text:
My earlier answer was incorrect: there is a rank-\(9\) counterexample on \(\mathbb P^5\). The minimum is
\[
\boxed{d=5}.
\]

### A counterexample on \(\mathbb P^5\)

Let \(V\) be a six-dimensional complex vector space, and let \(Q\) be the universal quotient bundle on \(\mathbb P(V)\):
\[
0\longrightarrow \mathcal O(-1)\longrightarrow V\otimes\mathcal O
\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0.
\]
Choose a nondegenerate bivector \(\omega\in\bigwedge^2V\). It defines a section of \(F=\bigwedge^2Q\). This section is nowhere zero: vanishing at \([v]\) would imply
\(\omega\in v\wedge V\), whereas every such bivector has rank at most \(2\).

Consequently its cokernel is a vector bundle:
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O
\xrightarrow{\ \omega\ }\bigwedge\nolimits^2Q
\longrightarrow E_\omega\longrightarrow0.
\]
Its rank is
\[
\operatorname{rk}E_\omega=\binom52-1=9<10.
\]

### Uniformity

A line \(L=\mathbb P(W)\), where \(\dim W=2\), has
\[
Q|_L\simeq\mathcal O_L(1)\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,4},
\qquad
F|_L\simeq\mathcal O_L(1)^{\,4}\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,6}.
\]
The component of the section \(\omega|_L\) in the trivial summand is its image in
\(\bigwedge^2(V/W)\). This image cannot vanish. Indeed, otherwise
\[
\omega\in W\wedge V,
\]
and a bivector in \(W\wedge V\) has rank at most \(4\), contradicting the nondegeneracy of \(\omega\).

Thus the section has a nonzero constant component on every line. Taking its quotient gives
\[
E_\omega|_L\simeq
\mathcal O_L(1)^{\,4}\oplus\mathcal O_L^{\,5}
\]
for every \(L\). Hence \(E_\omega\) is uniform.

### Non-homogeneity

The isomorphism class of \(E_\omega\), on the fixed projective space, determines the line \(\mathbb C\omega\subset\bigwedge^2V\). Here is one way to verify this.

For \(F=\bigwedge^2Q\), the standard homogeneous-bundle cohomology calculations give
\[
H^0(\operatorname{End}F)=\mathbb C,
\qquad
H^0(F^*)=H^1(F^*)=0.
\]
Applying \(\operatorname{Hom}(F,-)\) to the defining sequence therefore yields
\[
\operatorname{Hom}(F,E_\omega)=\mathbb C.
\]
If \(E_\omega\simeq E_{\omega'}\), their quotient maps from \(F\) must consequently agree up to scalar, so their kernels agree. Thus
\[
E_\omega\simeq E_{\omega'}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathbb C\omega=\mathbb C\omega'.
\]

Projective automorphisms act naturally on these bivectors. Since not every projective automorphism preserves \(\mathbb C\omega\), not every one preserves \(E_\omega\). Hence \(E_\omega\) is not homogeneous.

### Minimality

The low-dimensional classification theorems for uniform bundles give:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Projective space}&\text{Ranks for which every uniform bundle is homogeneous}\\ \hline
\mathbb P^2&r\le3\\
\mathbb P^3&r\le5\\
\mathbb P^4&r\le7 .
\end{array}
\]
These are precisely all ranks \(r<2n\) in dimensions \(2,3,4\). No smaller dimension therefore qualifies, while the construction above qualifies in dimension \(5\).

The established classification results imply that every uniform bundle is homogeneous in the following ranges:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Space}&\text{Rank range}\\ \hline
\mathbb P^2&r\le3\\
\mathbb P^3&r\le5\\
\mathbb P^4&r\le6 .
\end{array}
\]
The first two rows exclude all ranks \(r<2n\) in dimensions \(2\) and \(3\), so \(d\ge4\). The last row does **not** exclude rank \(7\) on \(\mathbb P^4\).

The rank-nine construction on \(\mathbb P^5\) is valid. Let \(V=\mathbb C^6\), let \(Q\) be the universal rank-five quotient bundle, and choose a nondegenerate bivector \(\omega\in\bigwedge^2V\). Define
\[

\xrightarrow{\omega}\bigwedge\nolimits^2Q
\longrightarrow E_\omega\longrightarrow0.
\]

\[
\left(\bigwedge\nolimits^2Q\right)|_L

\[

d=

\end{cases}
\]
